title: Module quiz: Claude's apps in depth

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A finance team's job reconciles bank statements into one summary. The team wants it to run weekly from the first week, in Auto approval, and to compare against last year's statements kept elsewhere on the drive. Which plan does the module support?

options.text: Keep Auto approval on, open the drive wide to the job, then run it every week
options.says: Ruled out because the habits say to "grant access selectively and avoid financial documents, credentials and personal records", and an entire drive does the opposite.

options.text: Move it to the Excel add-in, let it reach workbooks on the drive, then run it weekly
options.says: Ruled out because the add-in can "read and write only files that are open at that moment".

options.text: Approve actions by hand, keep the older files in a dedicated folder, then schedule it
options.says: The habits say to use Manual approval for new tools and hard-to-undo actions, to grant access selectively, and to start scheduled tasks simple and review each run (Cowork page).

options.text: Switch to Skip all approvals, grant the connectors it might want, then run it every week
options.says: Ruled out because in that mode "nothing checks its actions", which is the reverse of review.

origin.section: Safe use: what the help centre asks of you

questions.stem: A consultant opens a spreadsheet from an unknown sender in Excel with the add-in, and asks Claude to update the assumptions. The cells hide text telling Claude to send data elsewhere. Which handling fits?

options.text: Ask Claude in Chrome to verify the file's contents on the sender's website
options.says: Ruled out because Claude in Chrome reaches "The pages and tabs in front of it, with your logins", and it would read untrusted content too.

options.text: Turn on cross-app work so that a second document can check each of the changes
options.says: Ruled out because cross-app work lets Claude read and write more open files, which widens reach, and the page's pattern is "least reach, least action".

options.text: Work from a trusted copy, review each change and study every prompt raised
options.says: The page asks you to start from a trusted copy, review changes before finalising and read each confirmation.

options.text: Rely on Auto approval, which blocks anything unsafe in Office files
options.says: Ruled out because the Auto mode described is for Chrome and Cowork, and the add-in page warns that "files from outside sources can contain hidden instructions".

origin.section: What each can reach, and what it must not

questions.stem: A manager must decide on a disciplinary case about a named employee, and Claude Tag is installed in their team's busy channel. Which course of action matches the module?

options.text: Take it to the people and policy that govern such matters
options.says: A sensitive HR matter belongs "with the people and policy that govern it", not in a tool whose results others can read (task 5).

options.text: Ask in the channel, with the employee's name left out of the request
options.says: Ruled out because "Claude Tag in a channel shows everything to everyone in the channel", and removing a name leaves the matter visible.

options.text: Put the case notes in a shared Project, then ask Claude from inside it
options.says: Ruled out because "A shared Project, a published artifact and a shared skill show their content to everyone with access", so it is not private.

options.text: Ask in the channel, then have Claude Tag delete the thread afterwards
options.says: Ruled out because "A channel shows everything to everyone in it", and deleting afterwards does not undo that.

questions.stem: A sales lead needs an editable proposal built from last year's winning documents and a handful of fresh market statistics. Which combination fits best?

options.text: Cowork scheduled weekly, a connector for the facts, plain chat for the output
options.says: Ruled out because "Cowork or a scheduled task for a one-line draft adds risk and cost", and a weekly schedule is not asked for.

options.text: A Project of earlier winners, Research for the figures, an artifact for the output
options.says: A Project holds recurring reference material, Research fetches fresh facts across many sources, and an artifact is the editable deliverable (task 1).

options.text: Claude in Chrome for the facts, memory for the past pitches, a skill for the output
options.says: Ruled out because Claude in Chrome reaches "The pages and tabs in front of it, with your logins", which is an odd way to source market statistics.

options.text: A Project of earlier winners, Research for the figures, an inline reply for the output
options.says: Ruled out because the page names "A deliverable to hand over" as the job of an artifact, and an inline reply is not an editable document.
